title: Burst anchoring and equilibration notes
content:
Purpose:
- Quick personal log for the "anchoring + equilibration" experiments. Trying to capture behaviors I observed running microbursts into a warm KV-cache enabled worker pool and how latency 'anchors' and then decays back to steady-state.

Context / motivation:
- Prod-like workload: intermittent microbursts (10-60 reqs over ~200ms) sitting on top of baseline 20 qps. We care about p99 impact and how long the system takes to 'equilibrate' (return near baseline p95/p99).
- Hypothesis: short high-amplitude bursts create an "anchor" effect in the scheduler/queueing/packing logic that increases p99 well after the burst ends; anchor dissipates exponentially with some half-life determined by batch timeout and prefill heuristics.

Run environment (single-node baseline):
- Model: redwood-13b-8bit (quantized test build)
